bet.text: A full-width ground intake, one of the big things the team wanted in the redesign and did not have on its first robot.

cycle.text: When the claw is empty and the intake holds coral, the claw goes down, takes it and returns to stow. One button drives the robot to the reef and into position; the driver confirms the score.
1690 says both aimed to take the closest coral to the closest spot; a slower partner upset this until kept to a loading-station lane.

endgame.text: A powered climber, held out by an over-center four-bar linkage. The climber comes down with that linkage as the climb pulls.
1690 says 4414's last cycles in Einstein finals 2 and 3 each ended with two coral dropped and the climb missed.

gave_up.text: An analyst of the Einstein finals says the robot had no wrist to turn coral sideways. It stood coral up in L1, where fewer fit and each had to be placed without knocking others over.
The intake was the biggest question mark of the rebuild, because it had to be prototyped rather than solved mechanically.

changed.text: This is the team's second robot of the season. The funnel copies the first robot's intake as closely as possible, and the elevator tensions each belt run separately, unlike in 2023.
In the rebuild thread the team said algae had not been tried yet but that, in theory, the claw could do it if 2056's could.
At the championship the claw took algae and coral.

outcome.text: 59-8-0 in official play; won the Johnson division; championship finalist; pick 1 of the Johnson alliance on Einstein; ranked 19 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 100.23, Johnson).

solves.text: Collect hard coral from the ground, including coral that arrives vertically

facts.text: Hollow polycarbonate rollers with 3D printed end caps, for weight, similar to 254 in 2022
Star wheels, which the team found best on coral in testing through the season
A pivoting front roller accommodates coral that comes in vertically over the bumper
Best in a flow state, with the human player rolling coral into the back of the robot; the team says this takes room and took several matches to dial in

cost.text: It was the scariest part of the rebuild, with a lot of guesswork and prototyping

solves.text: Bring coral to where the claw picks it up

facts.text: Two X44 motors, one on either side, spin the coral in
Copied as closely as possible from the intake of the first robot, where it was prototyped

solves.text: Run smoothly without finding a gear pair that clocks both belts to the same spot

facts.text: Number of stages
Both the up and down runs of the belt are tensioned, with a ratchet on the back
A poster outside the team says the carriage has four ratchet plates, one for each end of the belts
COTS idlers (WCP-1472) replaced the printed ones of 2023; the team prefers metal to printed parts, above all on high-load subsystems

cost.text: Replying about its sideways elevator, the team says it used the backside coral function 0 times in championship eliminations and is not sure it was worth the complexity

functions.name: Arm
functions.type: rotary arm on the elevator carriage

facts.text: Driven by a 10 DP gear on a laser-cut plate with a 10 DP profile
Clamped to two X-contact bearings, about 6 in each, on the elevator carriage
The arm is a carbon fiber tube bought pre-cut

solves.text: Handle coral and algae with one manipulator

facts.text: Takes coral out of the polycarbonate funnel
Holds algae with what the team calls the super pinch
Asked whether the dimensions and gearing of its 2056-style claw were given to it or estimated, the team said it counted pixels in photos

cost.text: An analyst says it cannot turn coral sideways for L1
Grabbing the coral and the algae from the stacks at the same time was pictured but never quite worked

functions.name: Climber
functions.type: powered climber on an over-center four-bar

solves.text: Keep the cage from knocking the mechanism back and bouncing it off

facts.text: An over-center four-bar linkage holds the climber out until the climb pulls it down
Very similar to what many other top teams were running, the team says

functions.name: Piece tracking and auto drive
functions.type: three sensors, a state machine and automatic reef drive

solves.text: Make scoring on the reef as easy as possible for the driver

facts.text: Sensors on the robot
They sit in the funnel, the intake and the claw, and tell the robot where the coral is at all times
A profiled PID controller controls acceleration and velocity in the drive to the reef
All controls are on one driver controller
The team runs Motion Magic with almost the same constants on every subsystem and no feedforwards, and tends not to set gear ratios in the motor configuration, because that changes the constants
Forum posters say it runs WCP swerve; the team joked along and did not correct them

decisions.choice: Use star wheels on the intake
decisions.because: coral is not compliant, and star wheels tested best through the season

decisions.choice: Copy the funnel from the first robot's intake
decisions.because: its geometry had already been prototyped

decisions.choice: Tension the up and down belt runs separately with ratchets
decisions.because: it takes less guesswork and makes the system smoother
decisions.instead_of: trying gears with different clocking, as on the 2023 elevator

decisions.choice: Hold the climber out with an over-center linkage
decisions.because: the force of the cage hitting the climber would bounce it back

decisions.choice: Drive to the reef automatically with a profiled PID
decisions.because: the team wanted control of acceleration and velocity so it scores every time

decisions.choice: Share the reef algae with 1690 in eliminations
decisions.because: the time saved by one less algae each would probably be canceled by another robot cycling over them
